verdict: COMBINING THE THREE NO-PEEK PREDICTORS (K562, 126 held-out KOs, tide-removed specific-mover recall@50). Singles: TIDE 0.241, PHYS 0.373, LEARNED 0.398. Ensembles: PHYS+LEARNED 0.427, TIDE+PHYS+LEARNED 0.447, UNION-neighbours 0.373. ORACLE* ceiling 0.616. DECISIVE: best ensemble (tide+phys+learned) 0.447 vs best single (learned) 0.398 = +0.049. REAL (if modest) ENSEMBLE GAIN, and it SURVIVES THE CONTROL: fusing phys+learned 0.427 beats the shuffled-phys control 0.331 (+0.097), so the gain is genuine KO-specific COMPLEMENTARITY -- phys and learned select partly different behavioural neighbours and catch different specific movers -- not the generic z-fusion re-weighting that fooled nexus_wall. Combining closes more of the graph->oracle head-room (42% -> 55%) and is worth keeping as the deployed no-peek predictor. It does NOT reach the oracle -- the predictors still miss the same hard neighbours the oracle finds by peeking, so a genuinely orthogonal signal is still needed for the rest of the head-room. (Deployable no-peek number stays ~0.40; oracle ceiling ~0.62.) Same protocol as wall_learnsim; single cell type, single steady-state-mRNA readout.
